# CPU work and frametime spikes in 0.4.0

Preliminary measurements and user reports indicate around **0.5 ms lower CPU-side render time** from the optimizations, depending on the scene and setup. This is not a guaranteed saving or an isolated measurement of any one optional toggle. Quad Views still adds roughly **3–4 ms CPU frametime compared with no mod**. It is worthwhile only with enough CPU headroom; a CPU-limited system may run slower despite lower GPU time.

The two additional focus views still require LMU scene traversal and drawing. Existing captures measured about 2.05 ms elapsed wall time for both focus hooks, of which 1.99 ms was inside native scene rendering. These nested scopes include driver/runtime waits and do not establish a matched mod-on/off CPU cost.

Implemented reductions:

- Cached outer-bank validation no longer probes COM interfaces that the bank already retains with AddRef, when all native wrapper/container/vector/interface identities still match. New interfaces are validated before any COM call. The WARP regression drops from 31 memory probes to 20, including zero redundant retained-interface probes. Interleaved optimized synthetic tests measured around 3–4 microseconds saved per cached prepare; this is not a measured game frametime improvement.
- Hiding the benchmark overlay now stops GDI bitmap rendering and pixel publication. Measurement, recording and configuration continue. Showing it publishes fresh pixels on the next tick. The launcher also stops refreshing its preview when that page is hidden or the window is minimized.
- Explicit profiling adds `outer_lock0/1` and separate menu buckets to distinguish time waiting for the global XR state lock from the existing runtime-image `outer_wait0/1` measurement. These are inclusive wall times, not exclusive CPU utilization. Profiling off retains zero clock/GPU-query behavior.
- Fresh launcher settings disable diagnostics, benchmark/focus overlays, optional render experiments and startup update checks. Explicit saved opt-ins remain honored. Enable diagnostics explicitly for a profiling capture.
- Diagnostic disk writes and flushes run on a bounded worker queue. Repeated periodic logs use a ten-second frame gate after initial diagnostics; draw hooks read its cached value. An overloaded queue drops messages and reports counters instead of waiting for disk I/O.
- Runtime Begin, Locate, EndFrame and application/outer image ownership calls release the XR state lock while in flight. Reservations protect session and resource lifetime. Outer images are prefetched after Begin, and failed waits preserve acquisition for retry. The late-Begin Pimax normalization happens at the valid Locate boundary, before engine rendering.
- Active quad/VRS checks read atomic lifecycle snapshots instead of taking the state mutex.

Other candidates need evidence and lifecycle work: capture-end sorting, descriptor caching and native duplicate traversal/draw submission. Startup/teardown and diagnostic benchmark-overlay runtime operations still have separate locking work; this is not a claim that every OpenXR call is unlocked. Borrowed renderer/vector memory keeps its validation checks. Removing image waits, restoration or validation would risk invalid images and is not an optimization.

For a useful A/B, keep the replay, graphics, runtime, provider, focus/crop dimensions and overlay visibility identical. Compare diagnostics off first with external timing, then perform a separate diagnostic capture to identify the costly stage. Include median, p95/p99, spike frequency and whether the spike appears in native scene work, lock wait, image wait or provider submission.

## SPS and NVIDIA Multi-View Rendering

Single-pass instancing can reduce duplicate CPU draw submission; NVIDIA MVR can project a geometry stream into up to four views. Hardware capability alone does not eliminate LMU's native per-eye traversals. The portable offscreen two-eye proof and guarded shader conversion already work, but replacing native draws still needs a paired scheduler, compatible shaders, union visibility, eye-specific state and correctly owned render targets. Research-only MVR2/MVR4 shader conversion passes WARP checks, but is not connected to native game drawing.

The local RTX 5090 passes the existing portable hardware proof and reports NVAPI SPS/MVR support. This is not a live LMU speedup. The optional capability command in PortableStereoCheck queries support without enabling modes or changing the game.

Two subsequent experimental NVIDIA mode/readback tests returned `DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG`. A user-authorized repeat with no LMU process before or after the run reproduced the same error. LMU being open is therefore not necessary for this failure; prototype/API usage and the driver still need investigation. See the [research status](CPU-RESEARCH-20261105.md). No SPS/MVR game speedup or multi-millisecond CPU improvement is established.

References: [NVIDIA Single Pass Stereo](https://developer.nvidia.com/vrworks/graphics/singlepassstereo), [NVIDIA Multi-View Rendering](https://developer.nvidia.com/vrworks/graphics/multiview), [renderer implementation handoff](../INSTANCED-STEREO-HANDOFF.md).
